title: Baptized (9.6)
hook: with his son Adeodatus and his friend Alypius, at the water
tomorrow: what happens when a mother and son talk about heaven?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the garden: two verses, a book closed on a finger. Your line: all darkness vanished.

A baptism photo: a baby in white, held up for the camera. Augustine's baptism has a stranger detail. Standing beside him at the water is his friend Alypius, and his own son, Adeodatus. And Augustine writes that the boy was the same age as the two men, in grace. How can a father and his son be the same age?
screen: `A BABY IN WHITE.` → `A FATHER AND HIS SON AT THE WATER.` → `THE SAME AGE?`

segments.voice: First, where the boy came from. Augustine doesn't hide it: born of him in the flesh, of his sin. Then, turning to God: you made him well. He says the boy's mind outran many serious, learned men, and that he himself gave the boy nothing but the sin. The gift was God's. Second, the friend. Alypius, Augustine notes, had trained himself so hard that he walked barefoot on the frozen soil of Italy. That's one to tell a friend tonight. Third, the water. They give in their names in Milan and are baptized together. Augustine's line is short, in his Latin: et baptizati sumus, et fugit a nobis sollicitudo vitae praeteritae. We were baptized, and anxiety about our past life fled from us. Tradition adds that it was the Easter Vigil, with Ambrose baptizing; Augustine's chapter doesn't stop for it. Fourth, the puzzle solved. In grace, everyone at the font starts at the same moment. The father with the complicated past and the brilliant boy both come up out of the water new, the same age. After, he says, he wept at the hymns of the Church, the voices flowing into his ears and the truth into his heart. He adds, quietly, that God soon took the boy from this earth, and that he remembers him without fear for him.
screen: `YOU MADE HIM WELL.` · `BAREFOOT ON FROZEN GROUND.` · `ANXIETY FLED FROM US.` · `THE SAME AGE IN GRACE.` · then, large: `WITH HIS SON.`

segments.voice: Set a glass or bowl of water in front of you and look at it: the light on the surface, the stillness. If you're baptized, let it bring the day to mind, or what you've been told of it; if not, a beginning someone stood beside you for. If you pray, you can make the sign of the cross slowly.
Baptized. Augustine's chapter on the water, where he, his friend and his son stood the same age in grace.
With his son: at the font, a father and a boy began together, both new. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Adults are usually baptized into the Catholic Church at the Easter Vigil, after a time of preparation, and Catholics recall their own baptism when they bless themselves with holy water on entering a church.
